why_the_variables: With them two launches of the same episodes on one card gave identical traces; without them the first query's actions already differed by 0.005-0.013 and the episodes went their own way (measured 2026-11-12). No measurable cost in speed.

sources.what: openpi, as released: the models, the policies, the released LIBERO configs, and openpi-client from its packages/
sources.licence: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE); it also ships Gemma's terms of use (LICENSE_GEMMA.txt)

build: git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Physical-Intelligence/openpi && git -C openpi checkout 15a9616a00943ada6c20a0f158e3adb39df2ccac && git -C openpi submodule update --init --recursive
cd openpi && GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 uv sync   (openpi's README, 'Installation')
the interpreter is openpi/.venv/bin/python; nothing of this repository is installed in it: evaluation/run.py puts this checkout on the path beside it
check: python -c "import openpi, openpi_client, jax; print(openpi.__file__, jax.__version__)"   (the path printed lies in the openpi checkout; jax 0.5.3)

machine_variables.OPENPI_DATA_HOME: where openpi caches downloaded checkpoints and the tokenizer

tried_on_the_test_host_2026_11_16: with uv 0.13.7: uv fetched CPython 3.11.18 and resolved 279 packages; clone 33 s, uv sync 75 s; checkout and .venv 8.6 GB; the two submodules initialised as openpi's README says (whether the sync works without them was not tried)
the check imports openpi from the checkout's src/ and openpi_client from its packages/openpi-client/src/; jax 0.5.3; upstream's uv sync also installs its dev group, pytest among it
